newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper settles weaker after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper settles weaker after choppy session.

text.p: COMEX copper settled weaker after repeatedly failing to cling to gains made during the day despite only a modest hike in LME stocks and a surge in U.S. housing starts last month.
LME stocks rose 2,875 tonnes on Tuesday to 115,375 tonnes.

"The market was struggling to hold in the plus column - the LME stock increase was at the lower end of expectations but the market could not mount too much of a recovery after the selloff yesterday," said David Rinehimer of Smith Barney.
March COMEX went out 0.25 cent weaker at 96.40 cents per pound, traded 98.25 to 95.80 cents. December ended 1.25 cents down at 98.90 cents, the weakest spot close in almost a month.
Construction starts on new homes and apartments, a key copper consuming sector, jumped at the sharpest rate in more than a year during November, U.S. Commerce Dept said.
Starts rose 9.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted rate of 1.514 million units, compared to a revised drop of 5.1 percent in October.
The American Bureau of Metal Statistics said U.S. refined copper production and inventories in October rose to their highest so far this year at 185,900 short tons and 71,100 short tons respectively.
The cash to three months backwardation on LME was still at $50 to $55, about half of last Friday's level.
"The backwardation has come in quite a bit which would suggest some easing in near-term supply concerns," Rinehimer said.
